title: Locale in the URL
lead: By default the locale lives in a cookie and the URL never changes. Set routing: true and every locale except the default gets its own path prefix instead.
prefix_text: Spelled exactly like the locale, so locales: ['en-US', 'de-DE'] gives you /en-US/some/url. If you'd rather have /de/, name the locale de — there is no second mapping to keep in sync.
wiring_text: handle from Setup doesn't change: it already reads the URL prefix once routing is on. reroute goes in a separate, universal src/hooks.ts (not hooks.server.ts) — it strips the prefix before SvelteKit matches routes, so your route files need no [locale] directory.
url_text: reroute only decides which route a request matches; the URL itself keeps its prefix. So event.url, the url of a load function and page.url all read /de-DE/about, exactly what the browser shows. To compare against a route, use route.id (/about), which never carries the locale. That goes double for access checks in hooks: /de-DE/admin renders the same route as /admin, so a guard on event.url.pathname lets it through.
base_text: Set paths.base as usual: svelte-dialect/kit reads it on its own, and the locale prefix is looked for after the base rather than instead of it.
linking_text: Use localizeHref for internal links — a bare href would drop the locale on navigation. It prefixes with the current locale, and the default locale always gets the bare path. This is ordinary same-locale navigation, so it never needs a full page reload.
switch_text: setLocale already knows whether routing is on: with it, switching navigates to the same page under the new prefix — a full navigation on purpose, so the served document, the URL and the runtime agree.
prerender_text: A static build only renders what the crawler can reach, and nothing links to /ru/... from the default-locale pages it starts from. localizedEntries multiplies your entry paths across locales for prerender.entries — see the demo's own vite.config.ts for a working example.
meaning_text: The prefix outranks cookie and Accept-Language: a URL is an explicit request for a specific version of the page. The default locale has exactly one address — /de-DE/some/url when de-DE is the default answers 308 to /some/url. With detectOnBarePath: true, a document visit to /about whose cookie or Accept-Language says ru answers 307 to /ru/about instead — off by default. Without it the bare path keeps its address and renders the locale the cookie or Accept-Language picked, the browser language on a static site, and the default locale only when none of them names one you offer.
